title: Development of an inexpensive, simple purification method for ω-5 gliadin from wheat flour✰
author: Maeta, Tanaka, et al.

steps.title: Extract crude gliadin from flour
steps.instruction: Extract gliadin from 2.001 g of ‘Harukirari’ wheat flour using a standard gliadin extraction method to obtain 0.132 g crude gliadin (66.0 mg per g flour).

steps.title: Separate gliadin by A‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run 10 % acid‑polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (A‑PAGE) on crude gliadin fractions from ω‑5‑deficient wheat, ‘Harukirari’, and ‘Norin 61’; identify the band that appears only in ‘Harukirari’ as the putative ω‑5 gliadin.

steps.title: Excise target protein band
steps.instruction: Excise the identified band from the A‑PAGE gel for subsequent protein recovery.

steps.title: Attempt recovery with acid‑detergent
steps.instruction: Homogenize the excised gel slice in 5 % acetic acid containing 0.1 % n‑octyl β‑d‑glucoside and sonicate; note that this approach yields very low protein recovery.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 % acetic acid + 0.1 % n‑octyl β‑d‑glucoside to gel slice.

steps.title: Recover protein by electroelution
steps.instruction: Place the same gel slice in an electroelution apparatus and perform electroelution (as described in the original study) to elute the protein; collect the eluate.

steps.title: Confirm recovery by A‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run A‑PAGE on the electroeluted sample; confirm the presence of the target band, indicating successful recovery.

steps.title: Verify molecular weight by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run 10 % SDS‑PAGE including a protein molecular weight marker, 20 µg of reference ω‑5 gliadin purified by the previous method, and the electroeluted sample; verify a band at ≈55 kDa.

steps.title: Identify band by nano‑LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Excise the most intense SDS‑PAGE band from the collected sample and analyze it by nano‑LC‑MS/MS; confirm the protein is ω‑5 gliadin.

steps.title: Calculate recovered amount
steps.instruction: Estimate ω‑5 gliadin amount: from 2.001 g flour, crude gliadin is 0.132 g; ω‑5 gliadin constitutes 9.56 % (95.6 mg per g crude gliadin). Apply the measured recovery rate of 24.5 % ± 4.3 % (n = 4) to obtain 0.176 ± 0.031 mg per experiment, equivalent to 1.55 ± 0.27 mg per g flour (n = 4).
